issue: Micro-slicing a single event across too many scenes.
why: The actual badminton game is stretched across four separate scenes (5 joining, 6 playing, 7 water break, 8 finishing). This violates the density and variety lens by taking one thin situation and micro-slicing it to fill the scene count. These should be condensed to make room for distinct vignettes (e.g., the locker room, a club cafeteria, or walking out with her new friends).

issue: Ignores Maya's established Week 7 gym routine.
why: The scenes frame this as Maya needing to find a way to exercise indoors because she hates running in the cold, but the Story Bible establishes she has already been going to the gym every Wednesday since Week 7. It feels like she forgot her own schedule.

In Denmark, sports clubs (foreninger) are volunteer-run, and season memberships are always handled online (via systems like Holdsport); municipal hall clerks do not sell club memberships over the counter. To maintain Danish realism, Maya should pay a drop-in/Pay & Play fee or state she is there for a trial session (prøvetræning).

issue: Unnecessary named character added against the brief.
why: The brief specifically asks for Maya to hit it off with 'two friendly players, Kasper and Sara'. Introducing 'Emil' as a third named character clutters the A1 vocabulary load with an extra name; Maya can simply join Kasper, Sara, and an unnamed partner or opponent.

issue: Too many new names introduced at once.
why: Introducing Kasper, Sara, and Emil all in one sentence is a bit heavy on the cognitive load for an A1 learner. Since the brief only highlighted Kasper and Sara, the fourth person for doubles could just be an unnamed player.

Maya already goes to the gym on Wednesday evenings (established in Week 7). Having her jog to figure out how to exercise, and concluding that she 'prefers indoor sports', makes it sound like she is starting from scratch rather than just seeking a social sport to complement her existing indoor gym habit.
She pays for a full season membership before she has even seen the courts or met anyone to play with. Paying a drop-in or guest fee would feel much more natural for her very first night.
Maya takes the bus to the sports hall, but the hall is described as being 'in her neighborhood', which typically implies it is within walking distance.

The brief specifically asks to introduce Kasper and Sara. Giving the necessary third player a name (Emil) adds an extra character for the learner to track who will never appear again; he can simply be an unnamed fourth player to keep the focus on the recurring cast.
